draft.title: Bushfires
card: A bushfire is an uncontrolled fire in bush, forest or grassland. It needs fuel, such as dry leaves, bark, grass and twigs, plus heat and oxygen.
Bushfire risk is high when the weather is hot, dry and windy and the fuel is dry. Heat and dry air dry out the fuel. Wind pushes the flames and spreads the fire faster.
Fires threaten lives, homes and ecosystems. Smoke can harm health far from the fire, and animals and plants can lose their habitat.
Bushfires happen in many parts of Australia, but they are most common in south-eastern Australia in summer, when conditions are often hot and dry.
draft.remember: Bushfire risk is high when dry fuel meets hot, dry, windy weather.

a.q: Which set of conditions makes bushfire risk highest?
opts: Hot, dry and windy weather with dry fuel
Cool, damp and calm weather with dry fuel
Hot, dry and windy weather with wet fuel
Cool, dry and calm weather with damp fuel
a.why: Hot, dry air dries out the fuel, and wind spreads the flames quickly. Dry fuel with calm, cool weather is less risky because the fire is slower to start and spread.
a.clue: Think about weather that dries fuel and weather that spreads flames.

b.q: A forest near Bendigo in Victoria has had a mild, wet spring. Then a hot, dry summer day arrives with strong winds. Why is the fire risk high that day?
opts: Hot, dry weather has dried the fuel and wind spreads flames
Wet weather in spring has left the fuel too damp to burn
Strong winds blow fires out before they can spread
Summer is the only season when bushfires can start
b.why: Hot, dry weather dries the fuel, and strong wind spreads a fire fast. The wet spring does not lower the risk on this day, because the fuel has since dried out. Summer is when risk is highest in south-eastern Australia, but the card does not say fires can start only then.
b.clue: Look at what the weather is doing to the fuel on the day itself.

a.best: Hot, dry and windy weather with dry fuel

b.best: Hot, dry weather has dried the fuel and wind spreads flames

problems.detail: The card says bushfires are 'most common in south-eastern Australia in summer'. By number of fires and area burnt, fires are most frequent in northern Australia's tropical savannas, during the dry season (winter to spring). South-eastern Australia's summer fires are the most damaging to lives and homes, not the most common. Better: 'they are especially dangerous in south-eastern Australia in summer' or 'fire seasons differ across Australia'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer each. The card overstates that bushfires are 'most common' in south-eastern Australia in summer, when northern Australia's dry-season fires are more frequent; reword it to say they are especially dangerous there.
